tagline: A private, self-hosted health record — care team, appointments, symptoms, medications and imported clinical summaries — kept in Postgres on your own machine.
summary: My Health replaces the scatter of portal PDFs, notes and calendar invites with one dashboard. It tracks your **care team** (hospitals, specialties, doctors), **appointments**, a **journal** of focus areas and daily entries, and a **health record** of medical history events, symptom logs and research notes. A morning check-in logs symptom severity for last night, this morning and now.

It can import a hospital **Health Summary** (a C-CDA zip/XML export from patient portals): a wizard previews the file in memory and commits allergies, medications, conditions, vital signs, results, clinical notes, referrals and insurance into their own tables. Everything stays in local Postgres; the API binds to your machine and nothing is uploaded anywhere.
audience: You (or someone you care for) have many doctors and visits and want one place to see them.
Your patient portal can export a Health Summary / C-CDA package.
You want health data on your own machine, not in another cloud app.
notFor: Clinical use, diagnosis or sharing with providers — it's a personal record.
Syncing with Apple Health, wearables or portals automatically — imports are manual files.
Speech therapy and tube-feed tracking — those are moving to the separate speech-therapy-tracker project.

capabilities.title: Care team
capabilities.detail: `/hospitals`, `/specialties`, `/doctors` — doctors linked to facilities and specialties.

capabilities.title: Appointments
capabilities.detail: `/appointments` — visits with doctor, facility and date.

capabilities.title: Journal
capabilities.detail: `/focus-areas` and `/daily-entries` for what you're working on and daily notes.

capabilities.title: Morning check-in
capabilities.detail: `/morning-check-in` logs symptom severity and notes for three time windows; only rated rows are saved.

capabilities.title: Clinical import
capabilities.detail: `/health-import` wizard (upload → preview → done) for C-CDA zip/XML up to 25 MB, parsed in memory; `/health-imports` lists past imports.

components.name: Web app
components.owns: Landing, dashboard, all record screens, import wizard and docs. Calls `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`.

components.name: API
components.owns: Local Postgres `my_health` (`migrations/`), CRUD under `/api/data/*`, C-CDA import preview/commit, API docs catalog.

dataFlow: Create `my_health` and apply `migrations/setup.sql` (or numbered files); the API connects with `DATABASE_URL` at boot.
The web app calls `/api/data/<entity>` for every list and form.
Import: the zip/XML is uploaded to `POST /api/data/health-imports/preview` (memory only), parsed, shown for review, then committed into the clinical tables.

trust.title: Browser
trust.detail: Only the API URL and landing links.

trust.title: API (your machine)
trust.detail: Holds `DATABASE_URL`. Uploaded health files are parsed in memory, never written to disk.

trust.title: Postgres
trust.detail: All health data (PHI) lives in your local `my_health` database — back it up and protect your machine.

commonTasks.title: First-time setup
steps: On the **API Express** repo, **Set up local database** to create `my_health` and apply migrations (`seed.sql` adds sample rows).
Set `DATABASE_URL` in the API's Environment step.
Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` on the web to the API's real port.

commonTasks.title: Import a Health Summary
commonTasks.when: After a hospital visit or when you get a portal export.
steps: Download the Health Summary (C-CDA zip) from your patient portal.
Open `/health-import`, upload, review the preview and commit.
Check `/medications`, `/allergies` and the other clinical pages.

commonTasks.title: Log a visit
commonTasks.when: You booked or attended an appointment.
steps: Make sure the doctor and hospital exist on `/doctors` and `/hospitals`.
Add the appointment on `/appointments`; record notes in `/daily-entries` or `/medical-history-events`.

troubleshooting.symptom: Web shows errors on every page
troubleshooting.fix: The API isn't running or `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` points at the wrong port (default 3009; Hub may use 3032).
The file must be a C-CDA zip or XML under 25 MB; other portal formats aren't parsed.

troubleshooting.symptom: Errors about therapy or feed tables
troubleshooting.fix: Those features are being removed from this repo (uncommitted) and live in speech-therapy-tracker.

glossary.definition: Standard clinical document format used by patient portal Health Summary exports.
A health topic you're actively tracking in the journal.
One uploaded summary file and what was committed from it.

hubNotes: Both repos have large uncommitted changes removing therapy exercises and tube-feed tracking (~140 deleted files in web, ~120 in API) — they've moved to speech-therapy-tracker. Migrations 005–014 still create those tables.
The API defaults to port 3009 (shared with several projects); the registry says 3032.
`~/github/my-health/` also contains speech-therapy-tracker repos and an unrelated `your-health-dashboard` (Vite/Bun) folder.
